evidence_class: Mocked: fakeredis command queue, operation journal and execution registry, a fake server clock, a fixture network between worker and API, and an in process run of the worker helper standing in for kubectl exec; no Kubernetes API server, kubelet exec or live worker Pod was used.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.commands: KubernetesCommandTransport(queue, pods, runner, expires_in_ms, fallback_enabled) is the runtime CommandTransport for backend kubernetes carrying answer, drain and cancel; apply_operation issues the structured command into the SV2-LDG-05 CommandQueue keyed by the operation id with the execution generation and expiry, and the worker receives it over the authenticated command endpoint

observe_operation reconciles by the command id derived from the operation id: a stored command that matches the operation's execution, generation and payload digest is applied, a missing one is absent and may be issued again because issuing is idempotent per key, any mismatch is refused, an unavailable store is unknown

fallback(execution_id, command_id) delivers only an issued, unexpired command of the current occupant generation, only when the fallback is enabled, only for an envelope under 100000 characters, and only into the Pod swarm-<execution_id> in the client namespace carrying this swarm's owner label and the command's execution and generation labels; it runs the fixed helper argv python -m scripts.swarm_v2.worker.control with one mode and the encoded envelope, asks status first and delivers only on absent; it answers disabled, absent, the stored state, stale, too_large, refused, unavailable, ambiguous, queued or known
KubectlExec runs kubectl exec --namespace --container agent -- with an argv list and no shell; a timeout raises TimeoutError and a missing kubectl ConnectionError

sanitize_report withholds output over 65536 bytes whole, removes ESC and C1 escape sequences and other control characters except newline and tab, replaces invalid UTF-8, redacts secrets with the strict hooks.secrets patterns and bounds each report to 2048 characters before helper stdout and stderr are stored in worker-transport-reports

worker_transport_ambiguous_total(store, slug) counts helper calls per mode (status, deliver) whose reply was lost or did not match its exit code, command id, execution id and generation; it is a Redis hash per swarm, not yet an exported metric

scripts.swarm_v2.worker.control: encode and decode carry the command id, execution id, generation, kind, payload, payload digest and expiry as one URL safe base64 JSON argument; decode refuses wrong fields, a malformed command id, non integer generation or expiry and a payload digest mismatch

main(argv) is the only helper a controller may exec: status ENVELOPE answers queued, known or absent and deliver ENVELOPE queues a new, unexpired envelope into the worker inbox through a per process staging file and an exclusive link; both refuse an envelope for another execution or generation of this Pod's launch record, and every reply carries the command id with the Pod's own execution id and generation, and anything else is refused with exit 2 and one sorted JSON line carrying the reason

WorkerControl(transport, state_path, handlers, inbox) saves an inbox envelope as a received record marked inbox before acknowledging it over the authenticated endpoint, drops it when the server refuses that acknowledgement, and does not let it stop mutations until the server accepts it, so the fallback never bypasses server acceptance, expiry or the run once rule
scripts.swarm_v2.api.commands: CommandQueue.command_id(execution_id, key) names the id issue uses

supported_versions.kubernetes: kubectl exec into the agent container of an SV2-KUB-01 execution Pod; exercised only through the in process helper, no live release
supported_versions.redis: the SV2-LDG-05 worker command queue and the SV2-RUN-04 operation journal; commands issued before this package are read unchanged
supported_versions.compatibility: The local runtime, its command transports and the worker command endpoint are unchanged; the worker command and runtime command test modules pass with this branch (proofs run 38071968276). The transport registers only under backend kubernetes.

authority: The actor comes from Commands, which accepts only an authenticated operator or the current master incarnation, and the command queue issues only to the current occupant generation of the seat; a forged credential is refused before any write in case B. The fallback execs only into a Pod whose owner label is owner_for(slug) and whose execution and generation labels match the stored command; the helper refuses an envelope for another execution or generation of its own launch record. Kubernetes RBAC for pods/exec in the worker namespace bounds who can run the helper at all.
authoritative_objects: The worker command queue in Redis and the runtime operation journal are authoritative; the worker state file holds the worker's own run record. Helper reports, the ambiguity counts and the inbox files are observational or transient and may be dropped.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each ran twice with identical records and every case check held in proofs run 38073606119; the later commit only removes an unreachable leftover in the inbox collector, confirmed by the run named in validation.
states.accepted: Answers from the fixture reach the worker handler with the exact structured payload over HTTP and over the fallback helper; a drain over the fallback and a drain over HTTP each put their worker in no new mutations mode and complete on its checkpoint. Shell metacharacters stay message content and every helper argv is the fixed helper, a mode and one URL safe envelope. Refused envelopes for another execution or generation, a tampered payload and an expired command leave the inbox empty, and a corrected new request is delivered. A lost delivery reply is reconciled by a status probe with no second delivery, a worker restart after a lost completion reports without rerunning, a lost issue reply is reconciled by command id with one stored command, a superseded execution is answered stale, and its worker's checkpoint after succession is refused so the server keeps the drain accepted.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit; manifest.json hashes them.
states.externally_verified: None: no live API server, exec or G3 deployment was exercised.

validation.red: proofs run 38071702796 on the tests only commit f78dc848: collection of the Kubernetes command tests fails on the missing module and every new worker control test fails on the missing helper functions
validation.tests: proofs run 38073125527 at tested_commit: 274 passed across the Kubernetes commands, worker control, worker commands, runtime commands and Kubernetes runtime modules; only the case records, then regenerated, differed
validation.lint: ruff check and ruff format passed through python -m scripts.ci_prepush
validation.review: Round one: Spec reader eleven findings, Standards reader thirteen, all fixed or answered. Round two: fixed inbox records saved before acknowledgement and dropped on refusal, helper refusals carrying the Pod identity, C1 and ESC string sequences, the visible U+009B escape in the fixture, a superseded worker's refused checkpoint, and the shared MODES constant. Held with reasons: the rollback switch stays a constructor flag like SV2-KUB-02, the uncapped exec capture is a recorded limitation, and a pod read without metadata cannot come from the API server.

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct or switch the transport with fallback_enabled False: fallback answers disabled without reading the Pod or running exec, while apply_operation keeps issuing commands that the worker receives over the authenticated endpoint.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case B ends with the fallback disabled: the next answer is delivered over HTTP and the helper is not called.

remaining_limitations: The worker loop in the image does not yet construct WorkerControl with the helper inbox and state paths; the helper writes into /home/worker/commands, which the supervisor must wire when the worker command loop lands.
The fallback only delivers: acknowledgement and completion still need the authenticated endpoint, so a worker that cannot reach the controller holds a fallback command in its inbox until it expires.
The fallback switch is the fallback_enabled constructor argument, as SV2-KUB-02 does for creation; wiring it to controller configuration belongs to the controller deployment package.
The Pod name is derived from the execution id by the SV2-KUB-01 naming rule rather than read from the execution registry, whose runtime target still carries a placeholder.
Helper reports and ambiguity counts are kept in Redis per swarm and not exported as telemetry yet.
KubectlExec captures the whole helper output before sanitize_report withholds anything over 65536 bytes; the read itself is bounded only by the exec timeout.
The controller host needs kubectl and a pods/exec grant for the fallback; neither ships with this package.
